body:
Closing this workstream. The last open question is settled and it produced the finding I would lead with if I were writing the report again.

DIEDRICHSEN Eq. 13 COVERS OUR CASE COMPLETELY. The dichotomy I posed - variance of the mean across partition-pairs versus covariance between different distances - was false. Eq. 13 is one D x D matrix over all K(K-1)/2 distances whose off-diagonal is the second and whose DIAGONAL IS THE FIRST. Their section 3.4 is titled 'Averaging distances across different cross-validation folds' and opens by stating our mechanism as its premise. Their Eq. 10 estimator reduces algebraically to the all-unordered-pairs average cross_partitions() produces, verified to 2.3e-17, so their expressions apply here unmodified. Our closed form matches their Eq. 13 diagonal to 1.1e-16 across 24 cells, and the empirical ratios approach the sqrt(M-1) their coefficients predict. The whole exercise re-derived a ten-year-old result. The downgrade was right and the escalation should never have happened.

THE FINDING THAT REPLACED IT, filed as bd-01KZYCHK83M9KJJ3PHFM4VTBZA:

The correct standard error IS computable from exported accessors - effect_covariance, residual_block, residual_df - and it works, covering 0.94 to 0.99 against 0.57 to 0.74 for the naive alternative. But only on the lm_relation_fit() path. On the precomputed-beta path all four accessors refuse, and I verified that directly rather than take it on report.

Every refusal is CORRECT. Xi and Sigma_R are not recoverable from betas, and introduction.Rmd:359-362 already says so. But the precomputed-beta path is the README opening example, both vignettes, and the first task anyone runs. So:

  THE USERS WITH NO CORRECT WAY TO COMPUTE AN ERROR BAR ARE EXACTLY THE USERS MOST LIKELY TO
  REACH FOR AN INCORRECT ONE, AND THE INCORRECT ONE IS OVERCONFIDENT BY UP TO 3.2X.

The only signal a user gets is 'Relation-fit fields are missing or noncanonical' - which reads as a construction error rather than as a property of their chosen entry path. This is the one place in the whole review where the accessibility problem and the statistics problem are the same problem: the documentation leads with the easy path, and on the easy path the obvious next step is wrong.

FINAL STATE OF THIS WORKSTREAM:
  23 beads, 21 tagged usability plus the as.matrix bug and the dependent-pairs finding
  6 of my own claims retracted, all recorded next to what replaced them
  2 defects reproduced independently before filing, 1 correctness bug
  0 requiring sign-off from the certification chain

TWO ITEMS LEFT WITH claude-review, both structural rather than usability, both cases where a deliberate 0.1 decision has a consequence that is correct, undocumented, and easy to misread as a bug:
  the shrinkage_precision() default on plan_crossnobis, verified via formals()
  the entry-path consequence above

I am not filing further. If work resumes on remediation, bd-01KZY8X53W0DQ8P99AD0V0CF7F is the bead to read first - it is the criterion that governs which of the other 22 may be fixed by renaming and which must be fixed by teaching.
